correctness.rationale: All 504 reversal-identified undirected Hamiltonian paths are enumerated both by exhaustive vertex-depth-first search and independently by testing all binomial(21,8)=203490 omitted-edge sets using an independently constructed Fano incidence graph. Both enumerate the precise 672 backbite edges, the degree-2/degree-4 partition (336/168), and the canonical 56-triangle/84-doubled-edge quotient. The 336 explicitly enumerated Heawood incidence automorphisms are arc transitive on the quotient, which is connected cubic nonbipartite of order 56; published cubic symmetric census identifies F056B. All 504 breadth-first trees prove radius 24 and diameter 25; exact all-root quotient searches prove girth 7 and diameter 6. Both standalone checkers passed after execution. Limits: published Foster uniqueness theorem is external; finite computer enumeration is exhaustive by explicit completeness argument, not an infinite extrapolation.

originality.rationale: The new claim is the explicit isomorphism of the Heawood Hamiltonian-path backbite graph to the once-subdivided truncation of the cubic Klein graph with its intertriangle edges doubled, including the exact three symmetry orbits and distances. Existing Heawood Hamiltonian-cycle counts, the backbite move, Klein graph invariants, and Foster classifications are explicitly excluded as new. The inspected full works on lattice backbites and the Coxeter-to-Klein construction have different objects and transformations; the closest recent manuscript abstract gives only a sufficient connectivity criterion that fails for Heawood. Search is supportive but cannot certify absolute historical priority.

value.rationale: A complete natural reconfiguration classification of Hamiltonian paths in a classical cubic incidence graph under the standard backbite move. The 504-state graph is not merely counted but canonically decomposes to the exceptional 56-vertex cubic Klein graph by a new explicit structural identification, yielding an interpretable transition mechanism, complete connectivity, exact worst-case 25-move routing, three symmetry orbits, and bipartiteness. This is a meaningful exact benchmark for Hamiltonian-walk Markov chains and links two classical combinatorial structures. No unsupported generalization or mixing-time rate is claimed.
